sentiment.label: Mixed
sentiment.summary: Coverage of the debut is broadly constructive on demand and big-name backing, but the shares gave up much of their early pop and closed well below the opening trade amid a weak broader market.
points: Shares closed at $97.17, about 17% above the $83 IPO price but about 13% below the $111.50 first trade (CNBC, Yahoo Finance)
CNBC reports Melius Research initiated with a Buy rating and $155 target, and Vanda Research estimates retail net buying of about $250 million
CNBC says Nvidia plans a roughly $10 billion Class N purchase and Altimeter's Brad Gerstner plans a $5 billion investment
Yahoo Finance shows the stock at $96.00 in after-hours trading, and CNBC notes lawmakers renewed calls for AI regulation

updates.text: Anthropic's shares closed their first day on Nasdaq at $97.17, about 17% above the $83 IPO price but well below the $111.50 first trade and the intraday high of roughly $115.
CNBC reports that Nvidia has agreed to buy about $10 billion of Anthropic Class N stock in a private placement to follow the public offering.
CNBC cites Vanda Research as estimating retail net buying of about $250 million on the first day, roughly double the figure for SpaceX's debut.
CNBC's live coverage says Anthropic has become the tenth US tech company to reach a valuation of $1 trillion or more, with the market capitalisation put at nearly $2 trillion at the open.

CNBC reports that Altimeter founder Brad Gerstner plans a $5 billion investment in Anthropic, which he describes as a cornerstone position, while Menlo Ventures puts the value of its stake at about $25 billion.
CNBC cites sources saying retail investors received about 15% of the offering, short of the roughly 20% target, and that about half of institutional orders went unfilled.
CNBC reports that ANT's volume had passed 640 million shares by mid-session, more than SpaceX's 522 million on its debut day, making it the most actively traded stock on Nasdaq.
CNBC says Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley stand to earn roughly $550 million in fees from the offering, above the roughly $500 million banks earned on SpaceX's IPO.
Fox News notes that the S&P 500, Dow and Nasdaq Composite were each down more than 1% in the afternoon, and that underwriters have until 18 December to buy 147 million extra shares at $83.

CNBC's live blog says Melius Research has started coverage of Anthropic with a Buy rating and a $155 price target. It also reports that roughly half of institutional investors who placed orders received no allocation in the offering.

Shares slipped from an intraday high of $114.99 to about $101 by 12:31pm ET, according to MLQ, citing Nasdaq data. Around 484 million shares had changed hands, roughly half the number sold in the offering.

Anthropic's Class A shares began trading on Nasdaq at about 11:48am ET, opening at $111.50, 34% above the $83 IPO price. The stock debuted well over two hours after the opening bell, valuing the company at roughly $2 trillion.

Anthropic filed its final prospectus with the SEC on the morning of 19 November, confirming 980 million Class A shares at $83 (about $81.3bn). The sale is expected to close on 20 November, with a separate $26bn Class N share sale to seven tech companies to follow and a 30-day option for banks to buy up to 147 million more shares.

Khaleej Times reports that Anthropic is expected to join at least six major indexes, including the Nasdaq 100, within 5 to 15 days of listing, and that a separate $26 billion private sale with cornerstone investors is also planned.

Anthropic prices its IPO at $83 a share, above the $70–78 range, selling 980 million shares and raising $81.3 billion. Trading on Nasdaq under ANT is expected from 9:30am New York time on 19 November.
